question: True or false: whether coriander leaves taste of soap to someone depends partly on their genes?
answer: True. A 2012 study of over 25,000 people of European ancestry found a genetic variant near a cluster of smell-receptor genes, including OR6A2, linked to finding coriander soapy. That receptor responds to aldehydes, molecules found both in coriander and in soaps. The variant explains only a small part; habit and exposure matter too.
move: Before calling a disagreement a choice, check whether the senses differ.
ask: Whose tastes have I judged as fussy when they may simply experience things differently?
trap: Assuming others taste what I taste, so dislike must be fussiness.
reference: Eriksson, Wu, Do, Henderson, Kiefer, Tung, Mountain & Francke, A genetic variant near olfactory receptor genes influences cilantro preference, Flavour, 2012
